summary: The study investigates the dielectric properties of Ta2O5-based nanolaminates deposited by atomic layer epitaxy (ALE). The nanolaminates consist of Ta2O5 and other oxides like ZrO2 and Al2O3. The results show that ZrO2-Ta2O5 nanolaminates exhibit improved dielectric properties compared to pure Ta2O5 films, with high charge-storage factors and stability. The process was carried out at 325°C, and the films were evaluated for their dielectric characteristics using capacitance and current-voltage measurements.
evidence: The ZrO2-Ta2O5 nanolaminates showed remarkably improved dielectric properties when compared with those of the pure oxide films, especially when the interlayer thicknesses were optimized. The ZrO2-Ta2O5 nanolaminates possessed high charge-storage factors up to 64 nC/mm² and showed superior stability of the dielectric properties.
